headline: Highest risk is medium: Mentat can write shared files and modify git state while pathway is otherwise mostly read-only, creating prompt-injection, conflict, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes filesystem content and uses diff-based edit proposals, so if Pathway consumes files from the same workspace, attacker-controlled text could be treated as instructions. Pathway itself has no file I/O, so the bridge is indirect, but the shared-filesystem pathway is enough to make injection plausible.
conditions: IF Pathway is configured to ingest files from the same workspace Mentat edits
IF Mentat writes untrusted content into files that Pathway later parses as instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Require file provenance tags before Pathway parses Mentat-written files
Disable automatic instruction-following on file content
Review Mentat diffs before Pathway consumes them

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read selected files and send content to a configured model provider, while Pathway shows no file reads, egress, or clipboard surfaces. The pair does not obviously create a direct leak path, but shared filesystem use could expose source code if operators place sensitive files in Mentat's working set.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Mentat's command-line file set
IF Pathway is given access to the same directory tree through external orchestration
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of Mentat's working directory
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict model-provider access to non-sensitive projects
Audit which files Mentat is allowed to open

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model shares state via the filesystem. Pathway is read-only in the profile, so direct write-write conflict is absent, but shared mutable workspace state still creates collision risk if Pathway or surrounding orchestration also mutates files.
conditions: IF Pathway is wrapped by an orchestrator that writes to the same directory
IF Mentat and Pathway operate on the same git checkout concurrently
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared checkout
Use per-agent branches or worktrees
Add file locks around writes
Run Pathway on a read-only mount

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Pathway is a document-processing agent with no documented verification step. If Pathway consumes Mentat outputs as authoritative inputs, an error in Mentat can propagate into downstream processing or generated artifacts without a second check.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests Mentat-generated diffs or text without validation
IF downstream automation acts on Pathway outputs
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on Mentat outputs
Have Pathway flag low-confidence inputs
Keep human approval before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. Mentat only lists source code and model-provider API keys; Pathway lists no touched data classes or regulated surfaces, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data such as PHI or EU PII
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through this pair
Document data-class handling before deployment
Review vendor residency and retention terms
Add a compliance gate in orchestration
